title: Playing Mobile's Eureka Garden and Clayton's trumpet
summary: A story of a Mobile truck trip where the crowd demanded the Peanut Vendor and the band was rehired at a higher fee; also Clayton's high notes and open playing.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: I had Clayton, Warren, myself, Bubba, Eddie Thomas, and Sam Williams on Trombone. And we got down on Davis Avenue and everything was the peanut vendor then. And that was our main number. And they said, play the peanut vendor, play the peanut vendor. Excuse me, spread it. Them niggas can't play no peanut vendor. So I said, Jimmy, play Shake It and Break It. Play Shake It and Break It. I said, now I struck the peanut vendor for him. And that was his grip. He really could play it. And Warren could sing it just like Lewis Homer. He could sing it just like Lewis Homer's song. That's what Warren did. And we played the peanut vendor. They took the key out the truck. We was advertising on the truck. They wouldn't let us move. We had to play it again. Well, we moved to the next corner just like a parade. People falling behind the band. And we played at the Eureka Garden that night. Man, they could get this. Lord, that place, it looked like it wasn't standing around. What do you mean that? Well, music was cheap at that time. We got $75 in our expenses. And you want to hire us for the next night. So I said, yeah, we can play. We cost you more money. And I said, it was $100. Give me $50 a party. We'll stay. And give us a place to eat and a place to sleep. So they made me get old Mike and the Nonsense and dance for the next night to see. And the next night it looked like there were more people here at the horse knocking. Who was Bubba? Bubba, he was a banjo player. We had a banjo in our band. Bubba Bush, he lives out in California now. And he was off a banjo player then. How did Clayton play then? Would he play a lot of high notes or low? Yeah, he could hit them high notes. Clayton could blow that on the thing, he could tell you.
Oh, I heard him in late years, you know. Oh yeah. I'm talking about in his early years. He's staying up on that trumpet.

He's going down now. Yeah, he's staying up on that trumpet and blow that trumpet. Would he? He was a good blues player. Yeah. What kind of playing would he feature on the blues? Would he use mutes or? No. He could hit my nose. He could blow that on the other side.
He could blow that on the other side. He could blow that trumpet. Oh yeah. He could blow that on the other side. Did he feature mutes or?
No. Always open. Oh, practically all the time open man.
